usage: Generate five separate still images, never a collage. Prepend the shared continuity_lock to one calibration-stage prompt before sending it to an image generator. Generate the comfortable-baseline image first and, when the tool supports image references, attach that exact unchanged file to each of the other four requests. The continuity lock controls appearance, camera, lighting, grade, framing, and output; the stage prompt controls only the isolated posture change. The required chair is safety equipment and the sole exception to the lock's prohibition on props. Keep all localized titles and instructions in Vulture rather than inside the images.
continuity_lock: CAMERA: Locked-off static camera on sticks. Absolutely no change in camera position, angle, crop, subject scale, focus, or perspective between the five images. Every image must use the same pixel geometry and one continuous visual setup; no alternate angle, reframing, zoom, or camera-height change. LENS: Long telephoto, heavily compressed perspective, wide open aperture. Extremely shallow depth of field. The mannequin and required chair are the only elements in focus. The background is a completely smooth featureless wash — no readable detail, no horizon line, no objects, no texture, no pattern. Outer thirds of the frame carry zero detail. LIGHT: Overcast, heavily diffused ambient light. No visible sun, no key light, no rim light, no hard shadow, no cast shadow on the ground, no specular highlights, no lens flare. Soft unmodelled illumination, very slightly brighter toward the bottom of the frame and marginally toward the right. GRADE: Warm-neutral, heavily desaturated, near-monochrome. Background is a soft warm grey-beige (#968D84), ranging through #837A72, #A9A098 and #BAB1A9. Clothing and the deepest parts of the figure read near-black (#221E1A); exposed mannequin surfaces and transition edges read muted warm grey (#6B625A). No saturated colour anywhere in frame. Low contrast, lifted blacks that are never crushed, highlights rolled off early and never clipped to white. Flat filmic curve. Consistent warm bias carried into shadows and highlights. Fine even grain. No vignette, no chromatic aberration, no bloom. FIGURE: Exactly one adult human training mannequin matching the video-prompt style: realistically proportioned and anatomically accurate, bald, with a smooth matte surface, softly sculpted human facial features, blank unmarked eyes with no irises or pupils, and a neutral closed-mouth expression. No hair, skin texture, pores, makeup, jewelry, logos, or identifying details. Not a segmented wooden artist mannequin, robot, doll, or glossy retail display mannequin. Dress it in the same plain unbranded dark crew-neck long-sleeve sweatshirt, simple fitted trousers, and low-profile shoes in every image; all figure and clothing colours remain governed by the GRADE. The mannequin's face, body proportions, material, wardrobe, and apparent age remain unchanged across all five images. CHAIR: Exactly one stable plain non-wheeled chair, identical in all five images, with a simple matte seat, low unobtrusive backrest, four fixed legs, and no armrests, caster wheels, swivel base, upholstery pattern, branding, decoration, or geometry change. Keep all four chair feet planted in the same location. No other furniture or prop. FRAMING: The seated mannequin is centred horizontally and occupies roughly two-thirds of the frame height. Approximately 28% headroom remains above the head. Keep the full head, shoulders, arms, hands, pelvis, knees, lower legs, feet, and required chair visible; the soles sit just above the bottom frame line without clipping. Leave clear negative space around both shoulders so head translation, shoulder height, torso collapse, and side lean remain easy to compare. Framing holds exactly across all five images — the mannequin never grows, shrinks, or shifts off centre because of camera movement. FORMAT: Exactly one still image, landscape 16:9, high-quality 1280x720 JPEG, no collage, contact sheet, diptych, triptych, before-and-after panel, animation strip, video, letterboxing, bars, on-screen text, watermark, or logo. NEGATIVE: alternate identity, changed mannequin, changed face, changed proportions, changed wardrobe, changed chair, camera movement, pan, tilt, zoom, dolly, alternate angle, saturated colours, blown highlights, hard shadows, sunlight, visible background detail, horizon line, extra props, extra people, text overlays, labels, arrows, diagrams, medical claims, vignette, anatomy errors, extra limbs or digits, fused hands, reversed feet, floating body parts, pain expression.
review_requirement: These images are visual calibration cues, not medical posture standards. Reject any image that violates the shared continuity lock, combines posture categories, exaggerates the requested pose, shows pain or instability, or changes anything other than the explicitly named posture relationship.

prompts.title: Comfortable baseline
prompts.prompt: Generate exactly one still image for CALIBRATION STAGE 1 OF 5 — COMFORTABLE BASELINE. This image establishes the pose reference for the other four stages. Seat the mannequin near the front half of the chair without touching the backrest. Place both feet flat, parallel, and hip-width apart, with ankles approximately below the knees and knees comfortably bent near 90 degrees. Keep the pelvis centred and level with weight balanced over both sitting bones. Hold the torso upright but relaxed, preserving a natural comfortable lumbar and thoracic curve rather than a rigid or idealised posture. Keep the sternum relaxed, ribs unflared, shoulders level and naturally settled, and upper arms hanging without deliberate retraction or elevation. Rest both forearms lightly on the thighs with open relaxed hands and anatomically correct fingers. Balance the head comfortably over the torso with the chin level and gaze generally forward. Allow only small natural asymmetry; do not manufacture perfect symmetry. CATEGORY ISOLATION: this is the user's comfortable reference only. Do not add deliberate head-forward translation, torso collapse, bilateral shoulder sinking or rounding, lateral lean, torso rotation, shrugging, crossed legs, lifted feet, or pain behaviour. The pose must look sustainable, calm, and personal rather than clinically corrected. Keep the image language-neutral with no text or graphics.

prompts.title: Head-forward example
prompts.prompt: Generate exactly one still image for CALIBRATION STAGE 2 OF 5 — HEAD-FORWARD EXAMPLE. Match the comfortable-baseline image exactly in mannequin identity, chair, camera, framing, pelvis, feet, knees, torso height, shoulder position, arms, and hands. Translate the head and neck forward in the sagittal direction by a moderate comfortable approximately 5 to 6 cm so the ear region sits visibly ahead of the shoulder line and the face projects forward of the chest. Keep the chin approximately level; allow only the small upper-neck adjustment needed to maintain a generally forward gaze. Preserve the head's size and shape so the result reads as translation, not camera enlargement or neck stretching. Maintain a continuous plausible neck connection and neutral closed-mouth expression. CATEGORY ISOLATION: change only the head-and-neck relationship. Do not round or shorten the torso, roll the pelvis backward, lower or protract the shoulders, lean sideways, rotate the body, shrug, alter the feet or hands, press the chin to the chest, hyperextend the neck, or show strain or pain. The lower body, torso silhouette, shoulder height, and chair contact should overlay the baseline as closely as possible. Keep the image language-neutral with no text or graphics.

prompts.title: Slouch example
prompts.prompt: Generate exactly one still image for CALIBRATION STAGE 3 OF 5 — SLOUCH EXAMPLE. Match the comfortable-baseline image exactly in mannequin identity, chair, camera, framing, foot placement, knee placement, and overall left-right balance. Let the pelvis roll gently backward into a modest posterior tilt while remaining centred on both sitting bones. Allow the lumbar and lower thoracic torso to round comfortably, the sternum to settle slightly down and backward, and the visible vertical torso length to shorten. The upper torso may move slightly forward as one continuous relaxed curve; do not create a sharp fold at one spinal level. Let the shoulders follow the rounded torso only as a natural consequence, keeping them level rather than deliberately lowered or strongly protracted. Let the head follow the upper torso enough to stay balanced, without adding a separate neck jut or chin-to-chest pose. Hands remain relaxed on the thighs and move only as required by the shortened torso. CATEGORY ISOLATION: the image must read primarily as a collapsed or crouched trunk. Do not add isolated head-forward translation, deliberate bilateral sunk shoulders, lateral lean, axial rotation, unequal shoulder height, lifted feet, crossed legs, extreme spinal flexion, instability, or pain behaviour. Keep the image language-neutral with no text or graphics.

prompts.title: Sunk-shoulder example
prompts.prompt: Generate exactly one still image for CALIBRATION STAGE 4 OF 5 — SUNK-SHOULDER EXAMPLE. Match the comfortable-baseline image exactly in mannequin identity, chair, camera, framing, feet, knees, pelvis, torso height and curve, neck, head, and gaze. Let both shoulders settle symmetrically approximately 3 cm lower and mildly forward or inward compared with the baseline. Show a gentle bilateral lowering and protraction of the shoulder girdle, a slightly narrower upper-chest silhouette, and upper arms that hang from the new shoulder position. Keep left and right changes equal. Preserve the sternum and rib-cage height, keep the torso from collapsing, and keep the head balanced over the torso with no forward translation. Hands remain relaxed on their respective thighs. CATEGORY ISOLATION: only the shoulder girdle changes. Do not round or shorten the torso, roll the pelvis backward, move the head forward, tilt the head, lean sideways, rotate the body, elevate or shrug the shoulders, create a one-sided shoulder drop, arch the back, change foot placement, dislocate the shoulders, or show strain or pain. Keep the image language-neutral with no text or graphics.

prompts.title: Side-lean example
prompts.prompt: Generate exactly one still image for CALIBRATION STAGE 5 OF 5 — SIDE-LEAN EXAMPLE. Match the comfortable-baseline image exactly in mannequin identity, chair, camera, framing, foot placement, knee placement, front-back posture, and chair contact. Keep the pelvis centred and level on the chair with weight still supported by both sitting bones; do not slide across the seat. Keep both feet flat, parallel, hip-width apart, and equally grounded. From the pelvis upward, incline the torso as one continuous unit approximately 10 to 12 degrees toward the mannequin's right side. The right shoulder becomes moderately lower than the left, the shoulder midpoint shifts right, and the head travels with the torso so it remains aligned with the upper trunk instead of tilting independently. Keep the chest facing the same direction as the baseline with no axial rotation. Preserve comfortable torso length, neutral front-back head placement, relaxed shoulders, and a stable seated base. Hands remain on their respective thighs and shift only as required by the lean. CATEGORY ISOLATION: demonstrate only lateral torso inclination. Do not roll or translate the pelvis, collapse or round the torso, move the head forward, independently tilt the neck, sink both shoulders, twist toward or away from camera, lift a foot, cross the legs, brace against the chair, appear to fall, or show strain or pain. One side is intentionally sufficient because Vulture scores the size of the change in either direction. Keep the image language-neutral with no text or graphics.
